section_1.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
section_1.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'movement instructions' rather than just points. Establish the operations of scaling (stretching) and addition (tip-to-tail).
section_1.example: Imagine a Robot Scout. Vector v1 is '1 step North' and v2 is '1 step East'. Scaling 2*v1 means taking 2 steps North.

section_2.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
section_2.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling vectors and adding them together (a*v + b*w). Visually show the 'tip-to-tail' method on a 2D grid.
section_2.example: To reach a hidden treasure at (3, 2), our Robot uses a 'recipe': 3*(1 step East) + 2*(1 step North). This sum is a linear combination of the East and North vectors.

section_3.title: Span: The Reachable Map
section_3.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Use animation to show a line or plane being 'painted' as scalars vary from negative to positive infinity.
section_3.example: If the Robot only has one vector (East), its 'Span' is a single horizontal line. If it has East and North, its 'Span' is the entire 2D flat floor.

section_4.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
section_4.content: Explain linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can already be reached using the others (it's already in their span), it is dependent. Visually, show a third vector lying exactly on the plane created by two others.
section_4.example: Suppose the Robot has three movement vectors: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' vector is redundant because the Robot could already reach any point using just North and East. These three are 'Linearly Dependent'.

section_5.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
section_5.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are both linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space (can reach everywhere). It is the 'minimalist' set of instructions for a dimension.
section_5.example: For a 2D map, {North, East} is a basis. {North, East, North-East} is not (redundant). {North} is not (cannot reach East). A Basis is like a 'Standard Unit' that defines the grid.

outline.title: Span: The Reachable Map
outline.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Use animation to show a line or plane being 'painted' as scalars vary from negative to positive infinity.
outline.example: If the Robot only has one vector (East), its 'Span' is a single horizontal line. If it has East and North, its 'Span' is the entire 2D flat floor.

storyboard.title: Span: The Reachable Map
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all possible vector combinations.
One vector alone spans only a single line.
Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.
The span shows every location our robot can reach.
animations: Show vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 on the grid.
Draw a horizontal line in #AAAAAA to represent the span of v.
Add vector w (0,1) and shade the entire 2D plane in #444444.

outline.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
outline.content: Explain linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can already be reached using the others (it's already in their span), it is dependent. Visually, show a third vector lying exactly on the plane created by two others.
outline.example: Suppose the Robot has three movement vectors: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' vector is redundant because the Robot could already reach any point using just North and East. These three are 'Linearly Dependent'.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
lecture_lines: Linear dependence occurs when a vector adds no new directions.
If a vector is already in the span, it's redundant.
Three vectors on a flat floor are linearly dependent.
animations: Show vectors v (1,0) in #00FF00 and w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Highlight the 2D plane formed by the span of v and w.
Introduce vector u (1,1) in #FF0000 labeled 'North-East'.
Show u perfectly aligning with the sum of v + w.
Flash u, v, and w to indicate 'Linear Dependence' and redundancy.

outline.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
outline.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling vectors and adding them together (a*v + b*w). Visually show the 'tip-to-tail' method on a 2D grid.
outline.example: To reach a hidden treasure at (3, 2), our Robot uses a 'recipe': 3*(1 step East) + 2*(1 step North). This sum is a linear combination of the East and North vectors.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
lecture_lines: A linear combination scales vectors before adding them.
It's a recipe for reaching any point in space.
Our robot combines three steps east and two north.
This sum reaches the treasure at coordinate three, two.
animations: Create a 2D grid with the origin at center.
Draw vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 and vector w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Extend v to 3v (3,0) and w to 2w (0,2) on the grid.
Move 2w to the tip of 3v using tip-to-tail addition.
Draw the resultant vector (3,2) in #FF00FF labeled 'Linear Combination'.

outline.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
outline.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are both linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space (can reach everywhere). It is the 'minimalist' set of instructions for a dimension.
outline.example: For a 2D map, {North, East} is a basis. {North, East, North-East} is not (redundant). {North} is not (cannot reach East). A Basis is like a 'Standard Unit' that defines the grid.

storyboard.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
lecture_lines: A basis is a minimalist toolkit for a space.
It must span the space without any redundant vectors.
North and East form a perfect basis for 2D.
This efficient set defines our entire coordinate system.
animations: Show {North, East} vectors spanning the entire 2D grid.
Label the set as 'Linearly Independent' and 'Spanning 2D'.
Add vector 'North-East' and mark the set as 'Redundant'.
Show only vector 'North' and mark it as 'Insufficient Span'.
Highlight {North, East} in #FFFFFF as the 'Basis' toolkit.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper"
        lines = [
            "Linear dependence occurs when a vector adds no new directions.",
            "If a vector is already in the span, it's redundant.",
            "Three vectors on a flat floor are linearly dependent."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_v = "#00FF00"
        color_w = "#0000FF"
        color_u = "#FF0000"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show vectors v (1,0) in #00FF00 and w (0,1) in #0000FF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4, y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        
        v_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=color_v)
        w_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=color_w)
        v_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=color_v, font_size=24).next_to(v_vec.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("\\vec{w}", color=color_w, font_size=24).next_to(w_vec.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Group components for positioning
        visual_group = VGroup(plane, v_vec, w_vec, v_label, w_label)
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(w_vec), Write(w_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the 2D plane formed by the span of v and w.
        # Introduce vector u (1,1) in #FF0000 labeled 'North-East'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        span_rect = Rectangle(
            width=plane.x_length, height=plane.y_length, 
            fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.1, stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        u_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=color_u)
        u_label = Text("North-East", color=color_u, font_size=18).next_to(u_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(span_rect))
        self.play(GrowArrow(u_vec), Write(u_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show u perfectly aligning with the sum of v + w.
        # Flash u, v, and w to indicate 'Linear Dependence' and redundancy.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Temporary sum visualization
        w_phantom = w_vec.copy().set_opacity(0.4)
        # Move w to tip of v
        target_pos = plane.c2p(1, 0.5) # Center of arrow from (1,0) to (1,1)
        self.play(w_phantom.animate.move_to(target_pos), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Flash to indicate alignment
        self.play(Flash(u_vec.get_end(), color=color_u, line_length=0.3))
        self.play(Indicate(u_vec, color=color_u), Indicate(v_vec, color=color_v), Indicate(w_vec, color=color_w))
        
        # Redundancy text
        redundant_text = Text("REDUNDANT", color=color_u, font_size=20).next_to(u_label, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(redundant_text))
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis is a minimalist toolkit for a space.",
            "It must span the space without any redundant vectors.",
            "North and East form a perfect basis for 2D.",
            "This efficient set defines our entire coordinate system."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = [YELLOW, RED, BLUE, GREEN]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Grid Background
        grid_back = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRAY, "stroke_width": 1}
        ).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(grid_back, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Vectors: North and East
        v_north = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(0,2), buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        v_east = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(2,0), buff=0, color=BLUE)
        
        label_north = Text("North", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        label_east = Text("East", font_size=16, color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_north, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_east, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        labels_basis_1 = VGroup(
            Text("Linearly Independent", font_size=18, color=WHITE),
            Text("Spanning 2D", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(labels_basis_1, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(grid_back))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_north), GrowArrow(v_east))
        self.play(Write(label_north), Write(label_east))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels_basis_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1])
        )
        
        # Add North-East (Redundant)
        v_ne = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(2,2), buff=0, color=RED)
        label_redundant = Text("Redundant!", font_size=24, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label_redundant, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(labels_basis_1))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_ne), Write(label_redundant))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show Insufficient Span (Only North)
        label_insufficient = Text("Insufficient Span", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label_insufficient, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(v_ne), FadeOut(label_redundant),
            FadeOut(v_east), FadeOut(label_east)
        )
        self.play(Write(label_insufficient))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2])
        )
        
        # Restore North and East
        self.play(
            FadeOut(label_insufficient),
            FadeIn(v_east), FadeIn(label_east)
        )
        
        perfect_label = Text("Perfect Toolkit", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(perfect_label, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(perfect_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3])
        )
        
        # Highlight Basis
        self.play(
            v_north.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            v_east.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeOut(perfect_label)
        )
        
        final_label = Text("THE BASIS", font_size=32, color=WHITE).set_stroke(WHITE, width=1)
        self.place_at_grid(final_label, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)

    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title_text = "Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of vectors as movement instructions, not points.",
            "Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length.",
            "Adding vectors follows a simple tip-to-tail path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors matching the theme and animation elements
        COLOR_V1 = "#00FF00"  # Green for North
        COLOR_V2 = "#0000FF"  # Blue for East
        COLOR_SCALE = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow for Scaling
        COLOR_ADD = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta for Addition

        # Setup Coordinate System (NumberPlane) on the right side area (A1 to F6)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )

        self.add(plane)

        v1 = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_V1)
        v1_label = Text("North", font_size=20, color=COLOR_V1)
        v1_label.next_to(v1, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        v2 = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_V2)
        v2_label = Text("East", font_size=20, color=COLOR_V2)
        v2_label.next_to(v2, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(v1),
            Write(v1_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(v2),
            Write(v2_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length."

        v1_scaled_label.next_to(v1_scaled, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Transform(v1.copy(), v1_scaled),
            Write(v1_scaled_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Adding vectors follows a simple tip-to-tail path."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ADD))

        # Target position for v2 is from (0,1) to (1,1)
        v2_target_center = plane.c2p(0.5, 1) 
        
        v_sum = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_ADD)
        v_sum_label = Text("North + East", font_size=20, color=COLOR_ADD)
        # Position label carefully within grid area
        v_sum_label.next_to(v_sum, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            v2.animate.move_to(v2_target_center),
            v2_label.animate.next_to(plane.c2p(1, 1), DOWN, buff=0.1).scale(0.7),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(v_sum),
            Write(v_sum_label),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
section_1.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'movement instructions' rather than just points. Establish the operations of scaling (stretching) and addition (tip-to-tail).
section_1.example: Imagine a Robot Scout. Vector v1 is '1 step North' and v2 is '1 step East'. Scaling 2*v1 means taking 2 steps North.

section_2.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
section_2.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling vectors and adding them together (a*v + b*w). Visually show the 'tip-to-tail' method on a 2D grid.
section_2.example: To reach a hidden treasure at (3, 2), our Robot uses a 'recipe': 3*(1 step East) + 2*(1 step North). This sum is a linear combination of the East and North vectors.

section_3.title: Span: The Reachable Map
section_3.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Use animation to show a line or plane being 'painted' as scalars vary from negative to positive infinity.
section_3.example: If the Robot only has one vector (East), its 'Span' is a single horizontal line. If it has East and North, its 'Span' is the entire 2D flat floor.

section_4.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
section_4.content: Explain linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can already be reached using the others (it's already in their span), it is dependent. Visually, show a third vector lying exactly on the plane created by two others.
section_4.example: Suppose the Robot has three movement vectors: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' vector is redundant because the Robot could already reach any point using just North and East. These three are 'Linearly Dependent'.

section_5.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
section_5.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are both linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space (can reach everywhere). It is the 'minimalist' set of instructions for a dimension.
section_5.example: For a 2D map, {North, East} is a basis. {North, East, North-East} is not (redundant). {North} is not (cannot reach East). A Basis is like a 'Standard Unit' that defines the grid.

    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Span: The Reachable Map"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Span is the set of all possible vector combinations.",
            "One vector alone spans only a single line.",
            "Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.",
            "The span shows every location our robot can reach."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_V = "#00FF00"          # Green for vector v
        COLOR_W = "#FFFF00"          # Yellow for vector w
        COLOR_SPAN_LINE = "#AAAAAA"  # Gray for line span
        COLOR_SPAN_PLANE = "#444444" # Dark gray for plane span
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan for final span highlight

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Span is the set of all possible vector combinations."
        # Initialize the coordinate system and generic formula.
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        span_formula = MathTex(
            r"Span(\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}) = \{c_1\mathbf{v} + c_2\mathbf{w}\}", 
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(span_formula, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Write(span_formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "One vector alone spans only a single line."
        # Show vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 and a horizontal line in #AAAAAA.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_V))
        
        v_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_V)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}", color=COLOR_V, font_size=24).next_to(v_vec, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Horizontal line representing the span of v
        span_line = Line(axes.c2p(-3, 0), axes.c2p(3, 0), color=COLOR_SPAN_LINE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(v_vec),
            Write(v_label)
        )
        self.play(Create(span_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane."
        # Add vector w (0,1) and shade the entire 2D plane in #444444.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_W))
        
        w_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_W)
        w_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{w}", color=COLOR_W, font_size=24).next_to(w_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Shaded plane background (sized to match axes area)
        plane_shade = Rectangle(
            width=3.2, # 4.0 * 0.8 scale factor
            height=3.2,
            fill_color=COLOR_SPAN_PLANE,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(axes.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(w_vec),
            Write(w_label)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(plane_shade))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "The span shows every location our robot can reach."
        # Use Cyan to highlight the reachable area.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT),
            plane_shade.animate.set_fill(color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(plane_shade, color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        self.wait(2)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis is a minimalist toolkit for a space.",
            "It must span the space without any redundant vectors.",
            "North and East form a perfect basis for 2D.",
            "This efficient set defines our entire coordinate system."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = [YELLOW, RED, BLUE, GREEN]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Grid Background
        grid_back = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRAY, "stroke_width": 1}
        ).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(grid_back, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Vectors: North and East
        v_north = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(0,2), buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        v_east = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(2,0), buff=0, color=BLUE)
        
        label_north = Text("North", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        label_east = Text("East", font_size=16, color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_north, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_east, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        labels_basis_1 = VGroup(
            Text("Linearly Independent", font_size=18, color=WHITE),
            Text("Spanning 2D", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(labels_basis_1, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(grid_back))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_north), GrowArrow(v_east))
        self.play(Write(label_north), Write(label_east))
        self.play(FadeIn(labels_basis_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1])
        )
        
        # Add North-East (Redundant)
        v_ne = Arrow(start=grid_back.c2p(0,0), end=grid_back.c2p(2,2), buff=0, color=RED)
        label_redundant = Text("Redundant!", font_size=24, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(label_redundant, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(labels_basis_1))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_ne), Write(label_redundant))
        self.wait(1)

            FadeOut(v_east), FadeOut(label_east)
        )
        self.play(Write(label_insufficient))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2])
        )

        self.play(
            FadeOut(label_insufficient),
            FadeIn(v_east), FadeIn(label_east)
        )
        
        perfect_label = Text("Perfect Toolkit", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(perfect_label, "A4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(perfect_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3])
        )
        
        # Highlight Basis
        self.play(
            v_north.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            v_east.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeOut(perfect_label)
        )
        
        final_label = Text("THE BASIS", font_size=32, color=WHITE).set_stroke(WHITE, width=1)
        self.place_at_grid(final_label, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(final_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_north), Indicate(v_east))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Span: The Reachable Map
outline.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible linear combinations of a group of vectors. Use animation to show a line or plane being 'painted' as scalars vary from negative to positive infinity.
outline.example: If the Robot only has one vector (East), its 'Span' is a single horizontal line. If it has East and North, its 'Span' is the entire 2D flat floor.

storyboard.title: Span: The Reachable Map
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all possible vector combinations.
One vector alone spans only a single line.
Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.
The span shows every location our robot can reach.
animations: Show vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 on the grid alongside the robot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
Draw a horizontal line in #AAAAAA to represent the span of v.
Add vector w (0,1) and shade the entire 2D plane in #444444.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Span: The Reachable Map"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Span is the set of all possible vector combinations.",
            "One vector alone spans only a single line.",
            "Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane.",
            "The span shows every location our robot can reach."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_V = "#00FF00"          # Green for vector v
        COLOR_W = "#FFFF00"          # Yellow for vector w
        COLOR_SPAN_LINE = "#AAAAAA"  # Gray for line span
        COLOR_SPAN_PLANE = "#444444" # Dark gray for plane span
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan for final span highlight

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Span is the set of all possible vector combinations."
        # Initialize the coordinate system and generic formula.
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        span_formula = MathTex(
            r"Span(\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}) = \{c_1\mathbf{v} + c_2\mathbf{w}\}", 
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(span_formula, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Write(span_formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "One vector alone spans only a single line."
        # Show vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 and a horizontal line in #AAAAAA.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_V))
        
        v_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_V)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}", color=COLOR_V, font_size=24).next_to(v_vec, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Horizontal line representing the span of v
        span_line = Line(axes.c2p(-3, 0), axes.c2p(3, 0), color=COLOR_SPAN_LINE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(v_vec),
            Write(v_label)
        )
        self.play(Create(span_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Two non-parallel vectors can span an entire plane."
        # Add vector w (0,1) and shade the entire 2D plane in #444444.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_W))
        
        w_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_W)
        w_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{w}", color=COLOR_W, font_size=24).next_to(w_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Shaded plane background (sized to match axes area)
        plane_shade = Rectangle(
            width=3.2, # 4.0 * 0.8 scale factor
            height=3.2,
            fill_color=COLOR_SPAN_PLANE,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0
        ).move_to(axes.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(w_vec),
            Write(w_label)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(plane_shade))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "The span shows every location our robot can reach."
        # Use Cyan to highlight the reachable area.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT),
            plane_shade.animate.set_fill(color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, opacity=0.3)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(plane_shade, color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
outline.content: Briefly revisit vectors as 'movement instructions' rather than just points. Establish the operations of scaling (stretching) and addition (tip-to-tail).
outline.example: Imagine a Robot Scout. Vector v1 is '1 step North' and v2 is '1 step East'. Scaling 2*v1 means taking 2 steps North.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
lecture_lines: Think of vectors as movement instructions, not points.
Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its length.
Adding vectors follows a simple tip-to-tail path.
animations: Display vector v1 (0, 1) in #00FF00 labeled 'North'.
Display vector v2 (1, 0) in #0000FF labeled 'East'.
Scale v1 to 2*v1 (0, 2) in #FFFF00 to show stretching.

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

outline.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
outline.content: Explain linear dependence as 'redundancy.' If one vector can already be reached using the others (it's already in their span), it is dependent. Visually, show a third vector lying exactly on the plane created by two others.
outline.example: Suppose the Robot has three movement vectors: North, East, and North-East. The 'North-East' vector is redundant because the Robot could already reach any point using just North and East. These three are 'Linearly Dependent'.

storyboard.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
lecture_lines: Linear dependence occurs when a vector adds no new directions.
If a vector is already in the span, it's redundant.
Three vectors on a flat floor are linearly dependent.
animations: Show vectors v (1,0) in #00FF00 and w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Highlight the 2D plane formed by the span of v and w [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/floor.svg].
Introduce vector u (1,1) in #FF0000 labeled 'North-East'.
Show u perfectly aligning with the sum of v + w.
Flash u, v, and w to indicate 'Linear Dependence' and redundancy.

outline.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
outline.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are both linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space (can reach everywhere). It is the 'minimalist' set of instructions for a dimension.
outline.example: For a 2D map, {North, East} is a basis. {North, East, North-East} is not (redundant). {North} is not (cannot reach East). A Basis is like a 'Standard Unit' that defines the grid.

storyboard.title: The Basis: The Efficient Toolkit
lecture_lines: A basis is a minimalist toolkit for a space.
It must span the space without any redundant vectors.
North and East form a perfect basis for 2D.
This efficient set defines our entire coordinate system.

outline.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
outline.content: Define a linear combination as the result of scaling vectors and adding them together (a*v + b*w). Visually show the 'tip-to-tail' method on a 2D grid.
outline.example: To reach a hidden treasure at (3, 2), our Robot uses a 'recipe': 3*(1 step East) + 2*(1 step North). This sum is a linear combination of the East and North vectors.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: The Vector Recipe
lecture_lines: A linear combination scales vectors before adding them.
It's a recipe for reaching any point in space.
Our robot combines three steps east and two north.
This sum reaches the treasure at coordinate three, two.
animations: Create a 2D grid with the origin at center.
Draw vector v (1,0) in #00FF00 and vector w (0,1) in #0000FF.
Extend v to 3v (3,0) and w to 2w (0,2) on the grid.
Move 2w to the tip of 3v using tip-to-tail addition.
Draw the resultant vector (3,2) in #FF00FF labeled 'Linear Combination'.
